new_jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - EDA Algorithms
new_jobs.description:
**About Architect Labs**
------------------------

Architect Labs is advancing new frontiers in AI through silicon. Our goal is to compress end-to-end software to silicon timelines, and maximize intelligence per watt and per dollar for the world. Achieving this requires us to not only build our own radically competitive silicon products, but also reimagine how they are discovered, designed and produced at scale. We are a small exceptional team across silicon, systems, software and frontier AI. Our team has led research teams at nearly every frontier AI labs, and taped out some of the most complex SoCs in the world.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

A placer finishes twice as fast. The router spends the afternoon undoing its choices. Did the new algorithm buy us anything? You’ll have the blocks, the implementation flow, and the freedom to answer that question. Your job is to invent or accelerate physical design flows, tools and algorithms to change how we build chips end to end with AI, with focus on Place, Route, Clock tree, Synthesis, Hand off to Backend, power/timing estimations and over physical convergence.

* **Choose the research problem:** Identify, analyze and size every bottleneck with the physical design team, prioritize them and solve every one. It might be congestion that only becomes visible after routing, or a timing update expensive enough to rule out an otherwise promising search strategy.
* **Build the solver:** Own the algorithm, the flow, measurement and its implementation. That could mean a better objective for placement, an incremental graph update, or a parallel routing kernel. Profile it on real netlists and use what you learn to choose the next experiment.
* **Benchmark the full flow:** Give the incumbent tool a fair run. Match constraints and compute budgets, then follow the result through routing. Measure elapsed time, slack, area, and routability, including on the blocks where your method loses.
* **Put the algorithm/flow into production:** Work alongside the engineer closing the block. Make the solver reproducible, diagnose the corner cases together, and put it into the flow when the gains hold up.

**What We'd Like to See**
-------------------------

**Qualifications & Skills:**

* **Algorithm development:** You’ve implemented an algorithm for placement, routing, timing, or a related EDA problem. A dissertation, open-source tool, or commercial product can all demonstrate that experience.
* **Implementation depth:** You write performance-sensitive code and can explain how your choice of data structures or numerical methods affected runtime, memory use, and solution quality on larger designs.
* **Experimental judgment:** You design reproducible comparisons against strong baselines and can describe a case where a promising result failed to hold up downstream.The typo fixes from the last round (cover date, “Agrani Labs wins”, the double space) are still in place.
* **GPU Acceleration:** Experience accelerating placement, routing, or timing analysis with incremental methods or GPU parallelism.
* **AI for Physical Design:** Worked on numerical optimization, combinatorial solvers, or learned cost models for physical design.

**Bonus:**

* Experience working on industry standard tool development for Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens, etc - especially on digital physical design space.
* Experience working on research teams focused on AI for chip design, GPU-accelerated EDA tools for physical design etc.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

Competitive compensation, equity, and the opportunity to work on new tools, and methodologies to advance AI-driven physical design.

new_jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - Design for Test (DFT)
new_jobs.description:
**About Architect Labs**
------------------------

Architect Labs is advancing new frontiers in AI through silicon. Our goal is to compress end-to-end software to silicon timelines, and maximize intelligence per watt and per dollar for the world. Achieving this requires us to not only build our own radically competitive silicon products, but also reimagine how they are discovered, designed and produced at scale. We are a small exceptional team across silicon, systems, software and frontier AI. Our team has led research teams at nearly every frontier AI labs, and taped out some of the most complex SoCs in the world.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

When a part fails on the tester, how/what will we know about it? You’ll shape that answer long before tapeout. You’ll own the test architecture for all our silicons, make the case for the access and observability you need in RTL, and work with the test engineers who bring up the first parts.

* **Design the test architecture:** Decide how to reach every core and memory from the chip pins. Define the scan hierarchy, compression, test clocks, and memory built-in self-test, then carry those choices through full-chip integration.
* **Make testability decisions in RTL:** Work with RTL and physical design engineers on the hard trade-offs. A test point can recover coverage and cost timing on a critical path. You’ll measure both and decide with the block owner where it belongs.
* **Drive test signoff:** Own ATPG and DFT signoff. Generate and simulate stuck-at and transition patterns, explain the faults left uncovered, and close on a pattern set that fits the tester memory, test time, and capture power budgets.
* **Bring up first silicon:** Bring the patterns up with product and test engineering. When simulation passes and a part fails, use the fail log and scan diagnosis to narrow it to a pattern issue, a timing problem, or a silicon defect. Feed what you learn back into the next design.

**What We'd Like to See**
-------------------------

**Qualifications & Skills:**

* **Tapeout experience:** You’ve led and implemented DFT architecture, implementation and validation for multiple blocks and full-chips or, including scan insertion,BIST, ATPG, and gate-level pattern simulation.
* **Fault analysis:** You can trace a coverage gap back to RTL or constraints and explain which faults need a design change before signoff.
* **Tools and automation:** You’ve used Tessent, TestMAX, or Modus on a chip program and written Tcl or Python to automate insertion, pattern generation, or coverage reporting.

**Bonus:**

* First-silicon bring-up or volume failure diagnosis using tester data.
* Memory repair or hierarchical DFT integration across a complex SoC.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

Competitive compensation, equity, and responsibility for the test strategy from the first RTL review through the return of silicon.

**About Faropoint**  
  
Faropoint is a real estate investment firm that buys and operates industrial properties (smaller warehouses close to where people live and work) across 20+ U.S. markets. We run the firm on software we build ourselves: our in-house technology team builds the production apps our investment teams use to source, underwrite, and manage billions of dollars in real estate deals.  
  
**What We Build**

* FarOS, our deal platform and system of record, where every acquisition is sourced, underwritten, and tracked.
* REXy, our machine learning models that predict market rents, lease renewals, and sale prices.
* AI agents that read broker emails and offering memos and turn them into deals in FarOS, help prepare lease negotiations, and take routine work off people’s plates.
* The Faropoint Brain, our knowledge layer: an MCP server that gives Claude and our agents secure access to our leases, investment memos, data lake, and models.
* Slack apps and dozens of internal tools that bring all of this to where people already work.

**The Role**  
  
We’re a small team that ships fast. With AI coding agents, ideas go from a conversation with a user to production in days or weeks, not quarters. Writing code is no longer the hard part. The hard part is making sure what we ship is correct, tested, maintainable, and actually used.  
  
You’ll work day to day alongside a senior software engineer and a data engineer across FarOS, our data platform, and our AI tools. You’ll start with the work that makes those platforms solid: migrations, testing, bug fixes, and tech debt. As you learn the systems, you’ll build new features, agents, and integrations, and own more of the platform.

**What You’ll Do**
